cohort: Pregnant women in the Netherlands who experienced cardiac arrest during pregnancy or postpartum between 2013-2016
finding: The incidence of maternal cardiac arrest in the Netherlands was found to be higher than previous estimates, with pulmonary embolism, major obstetric hemorrhage, and amniotic fluid embolism being the leading causes.
mod_finding: Perimortem caesarean section was performed in 79% of cases where the pregnancy was at least 20 weeks gestation.
gest_age: Pregnancy and postpartum (up to 6 weeks after delivery)
